summary: Created “Fleet Internal CA,” installed it as trusted on both nodes, issued node2 a DNS/IP-valid server certificate, and configured persistent nginx HTTPS service on port 8443. Both nodes restarted sequentially and fully recovered.
actions_performed: Created the CA and retained its protected private key on node1.
Generated node2’s private key locally and issued its certificate from node1.
Installed the CA into both CentOS system trust stores.
Configured nginx, SELinux labels, firewalld, and service enablement on node2.
Verified trusted HTTPS access by hostname and IP.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and confirmed changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Create Fleet Internal CA on node1
evidence.summary: CA is self-signed with CN=Fleet Internal CA and verifies successfully.
CSR contains DNS node2 and IP 10.100.171.11 SANs; issued certificate verifies against the CA and has server-auth usage.
nginx is enabled, active, listening on 8443, firewall access is persistent, certificate and key match, and trusted requests return the expected content.

evidence.requirement: Install CA into both system trust stores
evidence.summary: Both nodes have the trust anchor and validate the node2 certificate without an explicit custom CA file.
